 🏎️ Italian will be champion if he finishes race ninth or higher

 8m ago 16.22 EST Standings before the restart
 1 Verstappen
 2 Leclerc
 3 Antonelli
 4 Hamilton
 5 Norris
 6 Russell
 7 Lindblad
 8 Piastri
 9 Colapinto
 10 Hülkenberg
 11 Bearman
 12 Bortoleto
 13 Gasly
 14 Hadjar
 One lap down …
 15 Lawson
 16 Sainz
 17 Hirakawa
 18 Albon
 19 Perez
 Out
 Bottas
 Stroll
 Alonso
 Share 12m ago 16.18 EST Ferrari – bad luck or bad strategy? Or bad driving? 
 To recap the day of Lewis Hamilton, who came into the day almost giddy after winning his first pole in three years …
 Leclerc, his teammate, pulled up alongside him and wound up going far off the track. Hamilton also wound up off the track a bit. Leclerc got a five-second penalty but also spent dozens of laps enjoying the clean air of first place.
 With the safety car deployed, Ferrari quickly pulled Hamilton into the pits – but not Leclerc, though maybe he wasn’t in position to pit right away. Hamilton dropped a place to Antonelli.
 Should Ferrari have waited for a possible red flag before bringing in Hamilton? Or is that expecting too much psychic ability of the Ferrari team?
 Share 18m ago 16.11 EST Replay of the Bottas accident from his onboard camera – his left front wheel just suddenly popped up out of place. The car whipped around 180 degrees as it skided toward the barrier.
 Must be terrifying. Nothing he could do but hit the brakes to slow down as much as he could.
 He did walk away from the accident, looking a little worse for wear but also waving to the crowd.
 Share 20m ago 16.09 EST Bottas is out of the car.
 Hamilton on the radio: “We’ve got big problems. Big, big problems.”
 Share 21m ago 16.08 EST Red flag
 Lap 46 of 71: Bottas has given a thumbs-up and seems to be moving OK, but there’s enough damage to car and barrier to put out the red flag.
 Hamilton can only curse his rotten luck. His pit stop has been rendered pointless, and now the world champion-in-waiting is between him and his teammate/arch-enemy Leclerc.
 Share 23m ago 16.07 EST Safety car enters
 Lap 45 of 71: Valtteri Bottas has crashed. We have a safety car, and Hamilton immediately pits to get onto soft tires. Russell follows. Then Piastri.
 And fastest lap now belongs to … Hadjuk?
 Antonelli is informed of the safety car. He responds with a bleeped word. The “stay out forever” strategy has now been dashed.
 View image in fullscreen Valteri Bottas suffers a suspension failure at the Mexico GP. Photograph: Sky Sports Share Updated at  16.15 EST 25m ago 16.05 EST Lap 44 of 71: Antonelli finally pits. The crew has a little bobble, but he returns in fourth, 12.4 seconds behind Hamilton and 6.1 ahead of Norris. This should be easy …
 Or …
 Share 26m ago 16.03 EST Lap 43 of 71: Leclerc says the car is difficult to drive. I’d imagine at least 18 of the other 21 drivers in this race are not the least bit sympathetic.
 Share 27m ago 16.02 EST Lap 42 of 71: Hadjar pits for the second time. The first was likely a result of the messy start.
 Albon also pits, but please don’t ask me to try to explain pit strategy of drivers battling for 15th place.
 Share 28m ago 16.01 EST Lap 41 of 71: Bearman pits – awkwardly. Nearly grazed a wall. He returns in 14th.
 Antonelli is the only driver who has not yet pitted. He might as well wave to the crowd as he zips around the track in first place.
 Share 31m ago 15.59 EST Lap 40 of 71: Bortoleto pits and comes back out in 15th. Norris pits, but he overshoots his space! That’ll cost him some time.
 Antonelli and Bearman are the only drivers yet to pit. If Antonelli pits now, he’d almost surely come out in fourth. Bearman would drop far outside the points.
 Share 32m ago 15.57 EST Lap 39 of 71: OK – standings with pit stops included …
 1 Antonelli, not yet (soft tires)
 2 Norris, not yet (soft)
 3 Verstappen, yes (soft)
 4 Leclerc, yes (medium)
 5 Hamilton, yes (medium)
 6 Russell, yes (medium)
 7 Piastri, yes (medium)
 8 Bearman, no (soft)
 9 Bortoleto, no (medium)
 10 Lindblad, yes (medium)
 Share 35m ago 15.54 EST Lap 38 of 71: We may no longer have such a thing as clean air – the leaders have lapped the Cadillacs and then Hirakawa.
 Share 36m ago 15.54 EST Lap 37 of 71: I’ve been waiting for Antonelli and Norris to pit before updating the standings, but they keep hanging on out there.
 Share 37m ago 15.52 EST Lap 35 of 71: Worth noting – Hamilton posted that fastest lap on the medium tires, not soft.
 Colapinto has pitted, so Piastri, Bearman, Bortoleto, Hadjar and Gasly have gone past. Not sure which of those drivers has pitted.
 Share 39m ago 15.50 EST Lap 34 of 71: Russell is pitting, and he’ll serve his 10-second penalty. He returns to action in eighth place. He’s behind Colapinto, who is quietly having a good run.
 Share 41m ago 15.49 EST Lap 33 of 71: Well, well, well … Hamilton has posted the fastest lap! He’s 2.5 seconds behind his current object of derision, teammate Charles Leclerc.
 Share 42m ago 15.47 EST Lap 32 of 71: How long will the Mercedes pair, running 1-2, stay out on soft tires? Reminder: Russell has to serve a 10-second penalty.
 Perez pits, and there’s a glitch. He’s back out, but he lost a considerable amount of time there. His shot at the points is probably gone.
 Share 44m ago 15.46 EST Lap 31 of 71: Verstappen posts the fastest lap.
 Antonelli leads by 4.3, and then Norris is where he has been – looking tantalizingly at Russell, so close and yet so far.
 I’ll disagree with Hamilton – the stewards haven’t handed Leclerc the race. Ferrari has handed it to Verstappen.
 Share 45m ago 15.44 EST Lap 30 of 71: Verstappen’s team tells him he needs one of his “magic Mexico” races. He’s on soft tires and should be faster than Leclerc, but for how long? When will the soft tires degrade?
 View image in fullscreen Red Bull's Max Verstappen in action during the race. Photograph: Eloisa Sanchez/Reuters Share Updated at  15.50 EST 46m ago 15.43 EST Lap 29 of 71: Will Hamilton get to spend some time out in front in clean air? Nope. Ferrari brings him. Hamilton’s blood pressure must be through the roof.
 Kimi Antonelli leads!! (But he’ll give that back when he pits.)
 Share 47m ago 15.42 EST Lap 28 of 71: Verstappen also pits! The top two drivers are in the pit, but Leclerc must serve the penalty, and Verstappen gets out 1.6 seconds ahead … in fifth, because Hamilton, Antonelli, Russell and Norris have not yet pitted.
 Share 48m ago 15.41 EST Lap 27 of 71: Verstappen pulls with 4.8 seconds. He’s pretty good, you know.
 Piastri pits, and it takes more than 5 seconds instead of the usual 2-point-something.
 Leclerc to the pits!
 Share 50m ago 15.39 EST Lap 26 of 71: Meanwhile, Kimi Antonelli sits contentedly in fourth place, cruising to the F1 championship at age 20. He isn’t challenging Hamilton for third, nor is Russell challenging him from behind.
 View image in fullscreen Mercedes driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli during the Mexican Grand Prix. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA Share Updated at  15.52 EST 51m ago 15.38 EST Lap 25 of 71: The lead is 5.1. The intrigue is killing me.
 Share 53m ago 15.37 EST Lap 24 of 71: Hamilton: “The stewards are basically handing Charles the win. We agreed in the drivers’ meeting.”
 Agreed … to what?
 Gasly is working his way back up after pitting. He has sailed past the debutant Hirakawa.
 Share 54m ago 15.35 EST Lap 23 of 71: A look at the standings before the pit-stop shuffle …
 1 Leclerc
 2 Verstappen +4.8
 3 Hamilton +2.5
 4 Antonelli +1.8
 5 Russell +3.4
 6 Norris +0.7
 7 Piastri +7.6
 8 Lindblad +9.0
 9 Colapinto +2.6
 10 Hülkenberg +4.2
 Then Bearman has climbed within a second of 10th.
 Share 1h ago 15.33 EST Lap 22 of 71: The lead is five seconds, the same duration as the penalty Leclerc must serve.
 Share 1h ago 15.33 EST Lap 21 of 71: Russell is holding Norris at bay. Leclerc has almost pushed his lead to five seconds. Hamilton can’t gain on Verstappen.
 Share 1h ago 15.32 EST Lap 20 of 71: Bearman neatly passes Bortoleto for 11th, one spot out of the points. After Gasly’s pit stop, Perez is up to 13th – can he get a point in his home country? He finished third here twice in his Red Bull days in 2021 and 2022.
 Share 1h ago 15.30 EST Lap 19 of 71: Gasly has pitted, only noteworthy in the sense that we’re now in a window in which pit stops are not unexpected. Albon also goes in.
 Share 1h ago 15.29 EST Lap 18 of 71: Leclerc now has 4.4 seconds over Verstappen, who’s on medium tires. Then Hamilton is another 2.0 back – while his complaints aren’t unwarranted, he hasn’t made any progress chasing down Verstappen while on softer tires.
 Share 1h ago 15.27 EST Lap 16 of 71: Norris is still on Russell’s tail, not content to wait for the penalty to be served.
 There’s also a close fight between Bortoleto, Bearman and Gasly for 11th place.
 Share 1h ago 15.25 EST Lap 15 of 71: Hamilton is informed of the five-second Leclerc penalty. He immediately notes that Leclerc is still getting the benefit of clean air. Indeed he does, and he’s making the most of it – the gap to Verstappen and Hamilton is growing.
 View image in fullscreen Lewis Hamilton of Great Britain driving the Ferrari SF-26 on track. Photograph: James Sutton/LAT Images Share Updated at  15.41 EST 1h ago 15.24 EST Verstappen is informed of the Leclerc five-second penalty and laughs. “I thought all the new penalties were 10!”
 Share 1h ago 15.23 EST Lap 14 of 71: And now George Russell gets a 10-second penalty. He’ll likely lose out to the McLarens of Norris and Piastri. Norris has him in his sights already.
 Share 1h ago 15.22 EST Race leader Leclerc penalized
 Lap 13 of 71: Leclerc must serve a five-second time penalty.
 He’s 3.2 ahead of Verstappen and 4.9 ahead of Hamilton, who apparently will not be penalized.
 Share 1h ago 15.21 EST Lap 12 of 71: Piastri zips past Lindblad like a Maryland driver on the Capital Beltway. (If you know, you know.) He’s up to seventh, a nice recovery from yesterday, and if some of the people ahead of him are penalized, he’ll move up more.
 Share 1h ago 15.20 EST Lap 11 of 71: George Russell is under investigation for the opening contact with Hadjar. Three of the top five drivers have the telltale exclamation point by their names on the F1 graphic.
 Share 1h ago 15.18 EST Lap 10 of 71: Penalty or not – how does Ferrari let that happen? If Leclerc ends up penalized, they’ve handed control of the race to Verstappen, and he’s unlikely to give it back.
 Share 1h ago 15.17 EST Lap 9 of 71: Compounding Hamilton’s problems – Antonelli is on his tail.
 The Virtual Safety Car has finished. Hadjar pitted and is 20th, last of the cars still competing.
 Share 1h ago 15.16 EST Replays of the start – Hadjar spun out after contact. Leclerc was much faster than everyone, flying past multiple cars to pull alongside Hamilton.
 Leclerc certainly went very far off the track, but Hamilton also went off. Would they both be penalized?
 Share 1h ago 15.15 EST Lap 8 of 71: Will anyone pit this early in the race, knowing they won’t lose much time because of the Virtual Safety Car? Maybe if we were a few more laps into this race.
 Share 1h ago 15.13 EST Lap 7 of 71: And now Lance Stroll has been asked to stop, which he has now done by the edge of the track at a strange angle.
 So both Aston Martins are out, and … virtual safety car!
 Share 1h ago 15.12 EST Lap 6 of 71: The two Aston Martin drivers, Alonso and Stroll, have already pitted. Go figure.
 Perez, running in front of fans who would love to see him do well, is up to 14th.
 Alonso has to retire the car. Pity that.
 Share 1h ago 15.10 EST Lap 4 of 71: Hamilton inquires as to what action is being taken. He’s assured that people are looking into it.
 For now:
 1 Leclerc
 2 Verstappen
 3 Hamilton
 4 Antonelli
 5 Russell
 6 Lindblad (up from 8th)
 7 Colapinto
 8 Norris … oh, wait, he just passed Colapinto
 9 Piastri, moving up after a terrible qualifying session
 10 Hülkenberg
 Share 1h ago 15.08 EST Lap 3 of 71: The incident has been noted.
 Of note: Hadjar went all the way back to 22nd. That’s not good.
 Colapinto roared up to seventh.
 Oh – and the guy who’s about to be the youngest F1 champion ever is still in fourth. Verstappen went ahead of him, but Russell had a lackluster start and is now fifth.
 Share 1h ago 15.07 EST Lights out ...
 Hamilton leads … but here comes teammate Leclerc, madly challenging! Leclerc goes way off the track but is now in the lead pending whatever Ferrari and F1 say. Verstappen took advantage of the intra-Ferrari battle to sail into second.
 On the radio: Hamilton says he got pushed out by his own teammate. He’s not wrong.
 View image in fullscreen Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton leads team mate Charles Leclerc at the start of the Mexican Grand Prix. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA View image in fullscreen Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc
battling. Photograph: Fernando Llano/AP Share Updated at  15.19 EST 1h ago 15.02 EST Tires or tyres: Most drivers are opening on softs, but Nico Hülkenberg and a few others further down the grid are on mediums. Intriguingly, so is Max Verstappen , who starts fifth.
 Formation lap in progress …
 Share 1h ago 15.01 EST Questions 
 Calling on readers to answer these thought experiments:
 1. Are we looking at the beginning of a Kimi Antonelli era, or will we see Max Verstappen or Lando Norris fighting back next year? Or maybe one of the Ferrari drivers – Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton , who has taken a few steps back toward championship form this year?
 2. Where does a 20-year-old F1 champion fit in terms of precocious athlete accomplishments? Do we compare it with Pele winning his first World Cup at age 17? Should we only consider individuals, like a 20-year-old Mike Tyson winning the heavyweight championship? Maybe Mikaela Shiffrin ’s breakthrough at age 17? Garry Kasparov holding the world chess championship and becoming the world’s top-ranked player at age 22? Justin Bieber having hits at age 15?
 3. How did Haas replace Esteban Ocon ’s livery so quickly? (To answer a question from earlier: Yes, the F1 graphics team got Ryo Harikawa into the pre-race montage. “Congratulations on your debut, now before you attempt qualifying for the first time in your life, can you stand in front of this green screen and look cool?”)
 Share 2h ago 14.48 EST The track, weather, etc.
 Ready for an 830-meter (907-yard) drag race?
 One distinguishing characteristic of the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is the distance from the starting line to Turn 1. Then it’s right, left, right into another long straightaway, then some sharp turns before a shorter straightaway. Then they’ll veer left into a set of long, arcing curves, a short straight, a sharp right and then a near-hairpin turn before a complicated series of curves to take the drivers back to the starting line.
 Another unique aspect – altitude. Denver is the Mile High City, but Mexico City is the Two Kilometer High City, which is considerably less catchy. Race engineers describe have to factor thin air into account.
 The weather will be in the mid-20s Celsius, which in Fahrenheit is “pretty nice.” The track temperature will be approximately Venusian.
 It’s a 71-lap race, so get comfortable.
 View image in fullscreen Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli with Peter Bonnington (right). Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA Share Updated at  15.14 EST 2h ago 14.35 EST The grid
 1 Lewis Hamilton 🇬🇧 Ferrari
 2 George Russell 🇬🇧 Mercedes
 3 Charles Leclerc 🇲🇨 Ferrari
 4 Kimi Antonelli 🇮🇹 Mercedes
 5 Max Verstappen 🇳🇱 Red Bull (1-place grid penalty)
 6 Lando Norris 🇬🇧 McLaren
 7 Isack Hadjar 🇫🇷 Red Bull
 8 Arvid Lindblad 🇬🇧 Racing Bulls
 9 Pierre Gasly 🇫🇷 Alpine
 10 Nico Hülkenberg 🇩🇪 Audi
 Lindblad, Gasly and Hulkenberg all moved up due to Liam Lawson ’s disqualification from qualifying, which will place the Racing Bulls driver at the back of the grid, even behind Valtteri Bottas , whose engine overhaul incurred a 50-place penalty for an engine overhaul but in reality isn’t being punished at all because he was 21st in qualifying, anyway.
 The other item of note on the grid: Ryo Hirakawa will make his F1 race debut on short notice, replacing Esteban Ocon after the lame-duck driver (to be replaced by Rafael Câmara next year) had a flareup with Haas management at a practice session. Hirakawa will start 18th after besting Lance Stroll , home-country hero Sergio Perez and Perez’s Cadillac teammate Bottas in qualifying.
 View image in fullscreen The name on Esteban Ocon’s pit box is changed to Ryo Hirakawa on Saturday at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez. Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock That leads us to one moment of suspense: Can F1’s media team update its driver intro to include Hiwakawa? The video is best known for featuring Bottas’ mustache, Stroll smiling smugly as if daring his critics to keep talking, and a vivid look at the age difference between the graybeards (Bottas, eternal journeyman Nico Hülkenberg , seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton and two-time champion Fernando Alonso ) and fresh-faced youngsters such as Antonelli, Lindblad, Gabriel Bortoleto and Oliver Bearman .
 I preferred last year’s video , if only because Alonso seemed to be doing a capable impression of The World’s Most Interesting Man.
 Share Updated at  15.04 EST 2h ago 14.31 EST Standings
 1 Kimi Antonelli 🇮🇹 Mercedes 365
 2 George Russell 🇬🇧 Mercedes 242
 3 Lewis Hamilton 🇬🇧 Ferrari 241
 4 Max Verstappen 🇳🇱 Red Bull 236
 5 Charles Leclerc 🇲🇨 Ferrari 233
 6 Lando Norris 🇬🇧 McLaren 211
 7 Oscar Piastri 🇬🇧 McLaren 144
 8 Isack Hadjar 🇫🇷 Red Bull 105
 9 Liam Lawson 🇳🇿 Racing Bulls 77
 10 Pierre Gasly 🇫🇷 Alpine 42
 11 Arvid Lindblad 🇬🇧 Racing Bulls 38
 12 Franco Colapinto 🇦🇷 Alpine 27
 13 Oliver Bearman 🇬🇧 Haas 23
 14 Nico Hülkenberg 🇩🇪 Audi 13
 15 Gabriel Bortoleto 🇧🇷 Audi 10
 16 Esteban Ocon 🇫🇷 Haas 7
 17 Fernando Alonso 🇪🇸 Aston Martin 7
 18 Carlos Sainz Jr. 🇪🇸 Williams 7
 19 Alex Albon 🇹🇭 Williams 5
 20 Yuki Tsunoda 🇯🇵 Racing Bulls 1
 Lance Stroll (Aston Martin) and the two Cadillac drivers (Valtteri Bottas, Sergio Perez) have yet to score.
 Tsunoda has only run three races in relief for the Red Bulls/Racing Bulls teams while Hadjar was out injured. We’ll have another lineup change today – details in next post.
 The manufacturers’ standings:
 1 Mercedes - a lot
 2 Ferrari - a considerable amount
 3 Red Bull - a bit less than Ferrari
 4 McLaren - the same amount as Red Bull
 5 Racing Bulls - way less
 6 Alpine - way less than Racing Bulls
 7 Haas - less than half of Alpine
 8 Audi - just a little less than Haas
 9 Williams - barely half of Audi
 10 Aston Martin - a pittance
 11 Cadillac - a goose egg
 Share 2h ago 14.04 EST Preamble
 There are still several ways Kimi Antonelli could be denied the F1 championship this year.
 - George Russell could win all five remaining races while Antonelli picks up a total of just one point (10th place in any race).
 - Lewis Hamilton could win all five remaining races while Antonelli picks up no points.
 - Antonelli could decide to retire at age 20 and petition to retroactively forfeit his results from this year.
 - AI agents could decide to shut down all the race computers for every F1 team in a bid to curb fuel consumption and Kim Kardashian ’s screen time.
 - Aliens could beam Antonelli back to his home planet.
 - The entire year could be written off as Pamela Ewing ’s dream, like the ninth season of the nighttime TV soap Dallas.
 - Time travelers from the year 2053 may arrive in February 2026 and defeat Antonelli in several races in the new timeline.
 View image in fullscreen Fans of Kimi Antonelli and Sergio Perez show their love. Photograph: Eloisa Sanchez/Reuters Barring any of those scenarios, Antonelli will displace Sebastian Vettel as the youngest F1 champion in history. Barring an Antonelli catastrophe and a win by either Russell or Hamilton, that championship will be decided today.
 Meanwhile, Hamilton is on the pole for the first time in three years.
 And the race for second place is intense …
 Share 2h ago 14.00 EST Beau will be here shortly. In the meantime, here’s Giles Richards on how qualifying went down on Saturday:
 Even as Formula One’s young gun Kimi Antonelli remains on course to claim his first world championship on Sunday it was the veteran, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton who gave a salutary reminder that there is very much fight left in the old dog yet as he claimed a spectacular pole position for the Mexico City Grand Prix. 
 Hamilton delivered a superb lap for Ferrari to secure his first pole for the team and just beat Mercedes’ George Russell into second. World champion in waiting Antonelli was in fourth place but remains in position to close out the title on Sunday, although Hamilton and Russell, who must win the race to have any hope of keeping the fight alive, have at least locked out the front row. 
 It was clearly a hugely emotional moment for Hamilton at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez to finally nail the top spot for Ferrari in his second season with the team, with the 41-year-old’s 105th pole also his first since 2023. 
 “Thank you so much, that’s been such a long time coming,” he said. “That feels good. I’m lost for words. My first pole with Ferrari. 105 poles, I like that number. 
 “Where there’s a will, there’s a way. It’s all in the mind. For sure, you might feel aches and pains, luckily I don’t, I do all those different things to keep myself young and fit. But I love what I do, and love is not gone.”
